children: Micron Technology (MU, Financials) is headed into its Sept. 30 earnings report with expectations high after the memory-chip maker's shares have soared almost 279% this year.

Wall Street is looking for sales of $50.91 billion in the fiscal fourth quarter, up almost 350% year over year, according to TipRanks. The company expects to earn $31.49 a share, compared with $3.03 in the same quarter last year.
That demand for memory used in artificial intelligence systems continues to exert pressure on supply and justify greater pricing.

Ahead of the release, Rosenblatt analyst Kevin Cassidy retained a Buy rating and $1,500 price objective. He's looking for another quarter of beat-and-raise and believes Micron's strategic client agreements will become even more important, possibly accounting for 40% of manufacturing bits in the next three to five years.
Cassidy also anticipates sequential growth in average selling prices in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 to support better gross margins.

Wolfe Research analyst Chris Caso also kept a Buy rating and $1,500 target. Demand for memory should exceed supply through at least 2028, aided by higher pricing for commodity memory and high-bandwidth memory, said Caso.

Micron stock increased 0.8% Thursday following a wild week that saw it climb 2.8% Monday and 5% Tuesday before sliding 2.2% The next catalyst is Sept. 30, when investors will be focused on Micron's pricing expectations, gross margins and if tight memory supply can continue into 2027 and beyond.

title: Micron's 279% Rally Is Heading Into a Big Earnings Test
